title: Micro-onboarding sprint review: quant & eval notes (Feb 02 2029)
body:
Attendees: Leah, Arjun, Sofia, Derek, Rina (brief drop-ins from infra: Tomas).

TL;DR: This sprint focused on (1) landing an int4 KV-prefetch variant for the 30B/70B onboarding path, (2) running a small-scale eval suite for generation quality on our standard prompt set, and (3) measuring end-to-end latency with microbatch=4. Early results: int4-KV reduces memory by ~3.2x and token cost by ~2.9x on our bench, with an average measured quality regression of ~1.9% (NLL/perplexity delta) on closed-book QA. Latency impact is modest (+6-12ms p50) when prefetch and background decoding are enabled.

Meeting notes / narrative:
- Background: goal for this micro-sprint is to validate a conservative int4 rollout path that preserves the existing KV cache semantics (no cache hash changes) and works with our canary routing policy. We prioritized quick experiments that map to a realistic Hosted API route (low sequence lengths, standard sampling).
- Experiments run (branch: feat/int4-kv-prefetch):
  * E1: int4 static quant (symmetric per-channel) without KV prefetch (baseline for quality).
  * E2: int4 + KV-prefetch enabled (prefetch the next 64 keys every request).
  * E3: int4 + background decode + microbatch=4 (throughput-focused).
  * E4: mixed-int (kv-int8, weights-int4) as a conservative variant.
  * Control: fp16 baseline (current production).
- Data & eval harness: used the onboarding prompt set (onboard-v2 — ~420 prompts, mixed short/long), closed-book QA subset (~120 examples) and our generation-robustness suite (typos/long-context). Evaluations were run via qbench-lite with deterministic seeds; artifacts uploaded to the mini-onboard confluence page.

Key results (summary numbers):
- Memory and cost: E2 shows ~3.2x working set reduction vs fp16 for 70B-ish configs; token cost estimates (infra sim) ~2.9x lower when accounting for batch packing improvements. E4 (mixed-int) is ~2.1x cost reduction with smaller quality loss.
- Quality: average perplexity delta (on closed-book QA) E1:+2.4%, E2:+1.9%, E4:+1.1% relative to fp16. For answer-exactness (EM) E2 dropped -1.7 absolute points on the small QA subset; E4 dropped -0.7. Observed failure modes: hallucinated numbers more often under int4 on numeric prompts; long-context coherence degraded slightly when past length > 1024 tokens.
- Latency/Throughput: baseline p50 token latency fp16 17.2ms. E2 p50 23.4ms with KV-prefetch warming (warm-cache); background decode reduces incremental p50 by ~4ms in E3 but adds scheduler complexity. Throughput (tokens/sec) improved with microbatch=4 for E3 (steady-state +18%).
- Stability & rollout readiness: E2 had one reproducible edge crash in the prefetcher when sequence length jumped from 128->2048 due to an off-by-one in the prefetch window; fixed in PR #203 (linked).

Operational notes / infra:
- Memory accounting: observed fragmentation in our memory allocator under int4 runs on the older kernel images. Tomas will try system allocator tweaks and report.
- Canary config proposal: start with mixed-int route (E4) for low-tier canaries (5% traffic) and a behind-the-scenes experiment for E2 with synthetic load. Need to expose route flags in the console: "int-variant=E4/E2".

Decisions taken in meeting:
- Proceed with a staged canary: E4 -> monitor quality metrics for 48h at 5% traffic; if stable, promote to 20% and run E2 experiments in isolation.
- Add a specific regression check to the eval pipeline: numeric-answer-verification (entity/number delta > threshold triggers fail).
- Merge the KV-prefetch crash fix and run a full canary smoke test before any external routing.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Are our current prompt sets representative enough for numeric-heavy workloads? (Sofia suggests adding the "finance-numeric" subset from the Customer Success repo).
- Do we need an explicit re-tokenization step for long-context cases before quantized runs?
- How will billing/token accounting reflect microbatching benefits — product to confirm expected customer cost changes. Linked ticket: MLON-612.

Action items (owner — due):
- Arjun: finalize E3 background-decode scheduling logic and add metrics for scheduler jitter (due 2029-02-09).
- Leah: add numeric-answer-verification probe to qbench-lite + run overnight (due 2029-02-05).
- Sofia: pull finance-numeric prompt subset into onboard-v2 and run short eval (due 2029-02-06).
- Derek: coordinate canary wiring with console team; expose int-variant toggle and rollout policy (due 2029-02-12).
- Rina: re-run full stable test on infra-kernel-5.19 image and report fragmentation numbers (due 2029-02-06).

Quick logs / snippets:
- AR: "E2 looks promising but watch the number hallucination; sample 74/120 failed with wrong numeric magnitude."
- LM: "Prefer E4 as initial canary because smaller quality delta and easier rollback."

Notes to self / followups:
- Capture a short demo video for the SRE rotation explaining the prefetch crash and fix.
- Add the EM/NLG metrics to daily dashboard and alert on delta > 2.0 for EM.

Appendix (short raw metrics):
- fp16 baseline: closed-QA EM=72.4, perplexity=18.2, p50 token latency=17.2ms, mem=100%
- E1 (int4 no-prefetch): EM=69.9, perplexity=18.7, p50=20.1ms, mem=31%
- E2 (int4 + prefetch): EM=70.7, perplexity=18.6, p50=23.4ms (warm), mem=31%
- E3 (int4 + background decode + microbatch4): EM=70.4, perplexity=18.8, p50=19.1ms (steady-state), tokens/sec +18%
- E4 (mixed-int): EM=71.7, perplexity=18.4, p50=18.0ms, mem=48%

References / links: PR 203 (fix prefetch crash), MLON-612 (canary billing question), confluence mini page (linked above), and onboard-v2 prompt list.

If anyone wants the raw qbench artifacts they're in the confluence page under "artifacts/2029-02-02" — ping me in #eng-applied-ml and I will share the GCS path.

End of notes.
